name: scrub-field
title: Scrub Field
description: A compact settings row of labelled number chips. Dragging a chip sideways changes its value, a bubble shows the change, and clicking the number lets you type an exact amount.
use: A settings or inspector panel needs precise numbers that are also quick to nudge by dragging.
avoid: Chips are fixed-width and dark by default, so they need colour props and overrides to fit a light toolbar.
a11y: The number field is a spinbutton with full key support, but the focused input has no visible outline. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: respected)
looks: A dark rounded panel headed SHADOW holds three stacked chips, each with a small label at the left and a right-aligned number with a unit. Beside it a rounded preview square casts a soft shadow that follows the values; while dragging, a small white bubble floats above the chip.
behaves: Pulling a chip sideways scrubs its number, easing past the limits with a rubber band and springing back on release while the bubble tracks the change. A plain click focuses the digits so you can type a value and confirm with Enter.
customise: Label, suffix, value, range, step, size, sensitivity, rubber reach, colours and the delta, fill and dirty toggles are props; the internal layout is fixed.
weight: light: Three chips with motion values; work happens only during a drag.
